what: Self-healing chains: a 2-hop chain with one standby exit, in network namespaces (tools/failover_lab.py). The primary exit's link is taken down mid-run while a prober inside the tunnel asks the destination every 250 ms which exit it sees; a second phase rotates sessions between live exits. The destination records every source address that ever reaches it.

setup.liveness: a paced link answers every tick; 3 s without an authenticated cell ends the session; a new session waits up to 2 s per candidate

reading.failover: Traffic flowed again through the standby exit 4.2 s after the primary went dark, in both runs; after recovery 184/184 and 180/181 probes succeeded.
reading.rotation: Over 300 s the sessions moved between the two exits four times, about every 93 s (window 60-90 s, aligned to 30 s session boundaries); the entry relay, the client's guard, never changed.
reading.leak: The destination only ever saw the two exits' addresses (and its own); the client's real address never reached it during the outage, the switch or rotation.

limits: Lab namespaces on one host; real-world reroute time adds the WAN round trips of the chain. Standby exits are single-chain (operator-run); mesh relays route per member and do not yet fail over between members' exits.
